title: Client SDK parity: bridging sync/async pagination, streaming, and retry semantics
creator: Ava Thompson
description: PRD for establishing consistent client SDK behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go for pagination, resumable streaming, and retry/backoff semantics. Goal: provide a small set of stable idiomatic APIs that preserve backward compatibility, enable deterministic resume semantics for long-lived streams, and guarantee predictable retry/idempotency contracts for common server-side error classes.
background: Multiple SDKs currently diverge in how they expose pagination cursors, handle resumable streaming, and apply retry/backoff policies (examples: Python iterator vs TS async iterator vs Go channels). This causes unexpected user migrations, duplicated retry logic in apps, and inconsistent observability signals. Customer feedback and internal support tickets indicate confusion around cursor expiry, partial-stream resume, and opaque retry windows. This PRD defines requirements, acceptance criteria, and a migration path for minimal breaking changes.
scope_included: Define canonical semantics and test matrix; API surface definitions for Python/TS/Go (sync and async variants); deterministic cursor token format and ttl guidance; streaming chunk boundaries and resume token handshake; client-side idempotency keys for at-least-once operations; default retry/backoff policy and configuration knobs; cross-SDK interop tests and CI gating; documentation and migration guide.
scope_out_of_scope: Changing server-side pagination formats or removing existing cursor fields; wide refactor of internal transport layers; language bindings outside Python/TS/Go; full rewrite of legacy SDKs—we will provide shims where necessary.
requirements: 1) Pagination: SDKs must expose a paginated iterator that supports resume_from(cursor) and returns stable cursor tokens. Cursor tokens must be opaque base64 strings containing schema version, resource id, and expiry. 2) Streaming: SDK streaming surfaces must support resume tokens emitted at chunk boundaries, and a handshake API to resume from a token with optional replay of the last chunk. 3) Retries: SDKs must implement a default retry policy for transient 5xx and network errors with exponential backoff, jitter, and a max-retries threshold. Users must be able to opt out and supply a custom RetryStrategy. 4) Idempotency: For user-initiated state-changing requests, SDKs will support an IdempotencyKey helper and attach deterministic client-generated keys. 5) Compatibility: New API variants must be additive; when unavoidable, provide a runtime compatibility mode (e.g., Client(enable_new_cursor_format=True)) and clear deprecation timeline. 6) Observability: SDKs should emit structured telemetry events for pagination/resume/retry decisions to integrate with Console tracing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit and integration tests: each SDK must pass the compatibility matrix (page-size variance, intermittent network failures, simulated server cursor expiry). 2) Resume correctness: resuming from an emitted resume token must continue iteration from the first non-duplicated item; optional last-chunk replay must be explicit. 3) Retry behavior: default policy retries transient failures up to N times (configurable), with measured 99th percentile latency within SLOs under injected failures. 4) Backwards compatibility: existing stable public methods remain unchanged or have compatibility flags; migration path documented. 5) Observability: pagination and retry events visible in Console dashboards for test tenants. 6) Polyglot tests: end-to-end scenario powering same workload across Python/TS/Go must produce identical item-sequence and cursor handoff behavior. 7) Documentation: PRD-linked migration guide with code examples and FAQ published before release.
test_plan:
- Create CI pipelines that run the polyglot interop harness (Python, TS, Go) against a test runtime that can inject faults.
- Tests: cursor roundtrip, resume-after-network-failure, resume-after-server-restart (persisted cursor), stream-resume-idempotency, retry-burst-stability (simulate rate-limited 429s), and telemetry emission checks.
- Performance: run load tests for pagination with variable page sizes and measure token cost per item and tail-latency.
- Release gating: all polyglot tests must be green; no new public method removals without compat flag enabled.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement compatibility shims in each SDK repo behind feature flags. 2) Release beta SDKs (opt-in) and doc migration guide; solicit early adopter feedback for 2 weeks. 3) Gradual opt-in by default for non-breaking improvements in next minor release. 4) Announce deprecation windows if any breaking change is needed, with tooling to detect usage of deprecated flows. 5) Post-release monitoring for two weeks with rollback plan to previous runtime if regressions detected.
migration_guide_summary: - For simple pagination users: replace next_page token usage with resume_from(token); tokens are opaque and must not be parsed. - For streaming consumers wanting resume guarantees: switch to the streaming.resume(resume_token, replay_last_chunk=True) call. - For custom retry: pass a RetryStrategy implementing backoff(jitter, max_retries) interface. - For language-specific tips: Python sync iterators map to TS async iterators; Go channels will expose a Close() that returns final cursor for resume.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Breaking user code if cursor format changes. Mitigation: Use versioned opaque tokens and default to legacy mode unless opt-in; provide detection tooling.
Risk: Inconsistent semantics across languages. Mitigation: Provide canonical behavior tests and a shared test harness.
Risk: Increased client complexity. Mitigation: keep API ergonomics simple, default to sensible config, and provide examples and migration snippets.
open_questions: 1) TTL for cursor tokens—recommended default 7 days vs 30 days? 2) Should resume tokens be signed by server to prevent tampering? 3) Exact default max-retries and base backoff constants—align with Console SLOs and cost targets. 4) How to surface server-side 'cursor invalid' errors vs 'cursor expired' to enable automated instrumented retries?
notes: Design reviews completed with Eng and Design on 2026-02-25. Engineering estimates include ~3 weeks per SDK for implementation plus cross-SDK test harness work. Plan assumes server support for emitting resume tokens at chunk boundaries. Coordination required with runtime team (ENG-50123) to standardize token schema.
